posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
Had a game go similarly unfairly against Akash'Bhuta during my game night tonight -- Argent Adept, Tempest, Ra, Fanatic and Haka against her in Insular Primalis. It took Akash three rounds to get any of her damaging cards out -- meanwhile, the Environment popped out three Obsidian Fields. AA got Syncopated Onslaught out early, Ra had both his staff and Solar Flare within a couple rounds, and Haka got the weapons out fast.

It amounted to everyone pounding the poor villain silly every turn directly and when she did get a limb out, it went down in a hurry and she did herself a heap of extra damage when it did. It was risky, sure -- the couple damaging environment cards that came out put the hurt on us and Ra knocked himself for a loop to keep Solar Flare out -- but I don't think I've ever seen a villain's HP drain that fast. I kinda felt sorry for her.

And this right after I told the gaming group that we'd need a solid buffer like Legacy because of how much HP Akash had. Silly me.

posts.cooked:
I think I have something to top the Cheap-Chart.

Legacy, DW Ex-Pat, G.I. Bunker and Wraith versus Voss in Megapolis.

Legacy Galvanized with Inspiring Presense out, and Roof Top Combat is in play with DW Aiming and Hairtrigger Reflexes in play. And bunker has Ammo Drop.

Voss gets out Forced deployment with at least 12 minions he can play.

I let Forced Deployment go off, releasing all of the minions with DW Ex-Pat killing each one as it's played with a +4 bonus for each attack.

If I keep letting Hairtrigger go off, I'm stuck in an infinate loop.

And for all the while Bunker just keeps getting cards...

Edit: Nope, not an infinite loop, just cycled through all the baddies. Still, quite an effective way to deal with Forced Deployment, isn't it?

posts.cooked:
Just discovered another fun trick against Akash -- Visionary + Wraith + Tempest + SST + Unity at Wagner base.

Use Visionary and Wraith to stack the top and bottom of Akash's deck with the limbs while Meteor Shower is out. SST forces them onto the field while Unity builds up her bots. Tempest uses Reclaim from the Deep to keep cycling Visionary's deck control cards, Unity's Construction Pylons, and Reclaim from the Deep itself.

Then take out the Meteor Shower (either by skipping a turn or with someone's environment destruction cards since by now you'll have several out). Unity gives Akash a double dose of Powered Shockwave, leaving Villainous Weaponry for last.

And then Platform and Raptor bots will usually finish her off.

Just as fun as End of Days with none of the bitter aftertaste of nuking your own stuff.
